docs.description: an effect declares no dependency array at all
docs.why: Without a deps array the effect re-runs after every single render, including renders caused by unrelated state. It is the one deps-array state no native rule inspects: `always-unstable-deps` and `missing-deps` both need an array to reason about, so this shape is invisible today. Note that the omission is sometimes deliberate — the latest-ref idiom (`useInsertionEffect(() => { ref.current = fn })`, a userland `useEffectEvent`) requires it — so treat this as a review trigger, not a defect claim.
docs.fix: Add the array: `[]` if the effect really is mount-only, otherwise what the body reads. If the omission is the latest-ref idiom, turn this rule off for the hook that implements it.
docs.example: useEffect(() => { document.title = title; })  // runs after every render

rules.message: this effect declares no dependency array — it re-runs after every render

docs.description: an effect's only dependency is provably stable, so it can never re-run
docs.why: A single dependency that the engine proves stable (a `useRef` container, a state setter, a module constant) can never change identity, so the effect fires once at mount and never again. Writing it as a reactive effect states an intent the code cannot honour — the feature the author expected to re-run silently does not.
docs.fix: If mount-only was intended, write `[]` and say so. If the effect should react to something, depend on the value that actually moves, not on the container that holds it.
docs.example: useEffect(() => { sync(ref.current) }, [ref])  // ref identity never changes

rules.message: the only dependency {dep.path} is {dep.stability} — this effect can never re-run after mount

docs.description: an effect unconditionally writes a state slot listed in its own dependency array
docs.why: The write changes a dep, which re-runs the effect, which writes again. When the write is proven to happen on every path through the effect body, the cycle has no exit — the component re-renders forever. Certified writes are reported as errors; writes the engine can only prove on some paths stay warnings.
docs.fix: Derive the value during render instead of storing it, or remove the slot from the deps array and write with the functional updater.

rules.message: this effect writes {setter.slot}, which is listed in its own dependency array

docs.description: an effect's dependency array exceeds the team's size budget
docs.why: A long dependency array almost always means one effect doing several unrelated jobs: every listed value re-runs all of the work, and the effect becomes impossible to review or to change safely. The budget is a review trigger, not a correctness claim.
docs.fix: Split the effect so each one owns a single concern and depends only on what that concern reads.
docs.example: useEffect(() => { /* fetch, subscribe, and sync the title */ }, [a, b, c, d, e, f])

rules.message: this effect declares more than {param.maxDeps} dependencies — split it by concern

docs.description: a custom hook the team has withdrawn is still being called
docs.why: Deprecating a hook by writing it in a migration document does not stop the next contributor — human or agent — from copying the nearest existing call site. Listing the withdrawn names here turns the convention into a gate.
docs.fix: Use the documented replacement. Update the `banned` option when the migration lands.
docs.example: const store = useLegacyStore()  // withdrawn: tears under concurrent rendering
